article_title: Neural mechanisms underlying the income-achievement gap: The role of the ventral visual stream.
citation: Rosen Maya L., Lurie Lucy A., Sambrook Kelly A., Meltzoff Andrew N., McLaughlin Katie A. (2021). Neural mechanisms underlying the income-achievement gap: The role of the ventral visual stream. Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dcn.2021.101025
title: VVS scaffolding model: cognitive stimulation shapes ventral visual stream development, which scaffolds prefrontal development, executive function, and academic achievement
description: The article tests a conceptual model in which "SES is associated with cognitive stimulation in the early home environment, which influences development of visual processing regions including the ventral visual stream (VVS)". Building on Amso and Scerif's framework, the model proposes that VVS "scaffolds the development of higher-order cognitive abilities through feedforward and feedback connections with the prefrontal cortex (PFC)", so that caregiver interactions highlighting visual features support semantic categorization, attention regulation, and ultimately EF and academic achievement. The study's mediation analyses offer preliminary support for this pathway.
requirements: Requires measures of SES, caregiver cognitive stimulation, VVS activation during attention tasks, EF, and academic achievement in the same children
constraints: The authors acknowledge several hypothesized associations were marginal and should be interpreted with caution until replicated; the study had only one neuroimaging time point and a predominantly white Seattle-area sample
target_learners: Children aged 6–8 beginning school from across the income distribution
examples: Caregivers highlighting features of objects that distinguish basic-level categories (e.g., a cat's pointed ears versus a dog's) as the kind of interaction hypothesized to support VVS development
